notes.title: This Week in Revan (May 28)
notes.content:
Since the last update, there haven't been any changes to the game world itself.. [i]however[/i], I am excited to announce that a new species is in development as both friend and foe. With a touch more detail, a long time twitch/youtube viewer of mine who dabbles in pixel art has decided to make some new assets for the generator of the engine along with some other odds and ends, such as minor tiles and new animations. Additionally, I have personally taken a crack or two at making edits to some of the onboard tilesets which will find their way into the game at some point in the future. 

But onto some fun news! We here at the hardytier household are welcoming Player 4 into the mix next Wednesday! This pretty much sums up why development has slowed down for the time being. Ideally this will pick up after birth.


Since I don't have any new patch notes for you, I'll give you an update on the short to mid-term goals. Keep in mind that this does not detail the [i]when[/i] of the releases. What I can say up front is the Orc War and An'ura Recon events will be in game and completely concluded before Scarlet Fire or any other "content" DLC are made.

- Kenmono cat creature NPCs find their way to Revan.
- Two more quests will be added to The Phoenix Ash.
- Bookcases in various homes across Revan will now contain helpful information about the game.
- The exit tiles of the Auria entrance zone will trigger the next step in the Orc War quest line. During the Orc War scenario, it will not be possible to return to the majority of previous zones in their current condition. A "passage of time" mechanic is currently in development to be a clear line as to when sidequests at hunter lodges can be completed.
- A new race of friend and enemy has found their way to Revan. 

[b]Fixes: [/b]

- Bugs will continue to be fixed upon their detection and rolled out immediately to Windows users. Mac users will have to wait for the next moderate update to receive these fixes. (This is because as far as I know, there are no active Mac players. If you are an active Mac player and need a fix for something, please reach out to me immediately as a comment to this post or on facebook @ facebook.com/CrossOfAuria )

notes.title: 3.2.3 - Changes from Friday's Stream
notes.content:
On Friday, I spent most of the time working on the next steps of the An'ura Recon questline. Specifically, fully creating and making live the next step of the quest and designing several skills for a new character which involved hours of testing and tweaking. If I'm going to give you an archer, he's going to do cool things. The VOD for this will be available on the CoA youtube channel within the next 24 hours. I'm piecing both small streams together and removing some of the down time where I had to walk away.

In addition to the progression of the quest, I found it necessary to dramatically scale back the level of the enemies in the Encampment. Based on my most recent test, a new player [i]could [/i]get to the end of the current main campaign at level 8. Sidequests from the Rabbit's Foot and Agartha would push a player to 20, but I won't rely on that for these side stories. 

- [b]Build already released on May 15th.[/b] I had every intention to make another update before this post, but I was sidetracked creating a rewards system and harvesting new assets.

[b][u]The Rewards System[/u][/b]
- Full details in the #coa_rewards channel of my discord. Invite link here: https://discord.gg/JcxZmeG
- Channel points accumulated from watching me on Twitch will now be used to make your own additions to the game! The details are still being worked out, but the highlights of this system are:
-- X points to create an NPC, the dialogue of which you may control if you want. Creation of an NPC or enemy involves hopping in a private discord call with me to make it in the engine generator.
-- X points to create an enemy, the backstory (of the days leading up to this character encountering the party) of which you may write given the existing lore of the world. You must also create at least 3 notable battle attacks for this character.
-- 100,000 points to create pretty much whatever you want, be it a small zone, a non-canon event, a playable character, etc.

[b]Please keep in mind[/b] this will be one of the only times I mention this reward system here on Steam forums, as it has more to do with Twitch than it does with communicating with the players. If you're interested in participating, please join the Discord and coordinate there.  
-- Points are obtained and exchanged on my personal twitch, @ twitch.tv/hardytier 

[b]Note[/b]: If you know how to make pixel art and want to inject an NPC into the game without using the generator, this does not cost points. You will need to provide a 3x4 sprite sheet of 48x48 px images, a name for the character, what they've been doing up until the party meets them, and an idea for what you want them to do moving forward. More specific detail to be discussed in discord. Keep in mind, this offer is only valid for non combat NPCs and for static enemy battlers only.

 [u][b]https://www.twitch.tv/hardytier[/b][/u]  is my personal twitch where the live streams will take place.

[u][b]Mac[/b][/u]
Earlier this week, we talked a little bit about functionality for MAC (see thread here: https://steamcommunity.com/games/764180/announcements/detail/2211773821814366841). Today, I'm going to follow up on that with some hopeful information.

It seems that it is possible for me to continue to make exports for mac in a different way than I do for Windows. However, it is greatly time consuming as I originally predicted. For that reason, the store page for CoAE1 has had Mac support unlisted for the time being. That being said, Mac players will still receive periodic updates, but not on the same time-frame as Windows users. Usually whenever an issue comes up, I jump to patch it right away - this won't be the case for issues on Mac. Instead, I'll be looking at monthly or even story based checkpoints for Mac only. Where Windows might see 3.3, 3.3.1, 3.3.2, and 3.4, Mac users may only see 3.3 and 3.4. 

Some quick notes:
- The current MAC build is 3.2.1.2, which is an extension of the 3.2.1 build (notes here: https://steamcommunity.com/games/764180/announcements/detail/2211773821813899258) but with the added bonus of the ninja patch which is available to all.

My depots were setup improperly which called for Mac users to download the windows only "www" folder, which is basically all the contents of the .app package an entire second time. [u][b]Linux[/b][/u]

I don't have a way to test this on my own, but the engine suggests that all the files are included within the package. As you may know, official support was discontinued many months ago due to my inability to test or understand it. With any luck, I'll be able to change that when the game enters post production.  

[u][b]
Other[/b][/u]
- On the whole, there hasn't been any other development yet this week. I'm focusing a lot on my projects for youtube for right now. That being said, I usually get most of my work done for CoA on Saturday mornings. When I do get back to it, I'll be continuing mostly on the new Orc War campaign, so there may not be another update again until next weekend. 

- Due to the frustration of trying to fix issues for Mac users this morning, the x. Patch Notes file has been left in disarray, but this gives you a chance to see what I have planned in a more detailed look if you want to see it. As always, these things can change. 

- I need to make a MAC version of the demo first and foremost this weekend, so this will take up some of my scheduled development time. When I made it, I was unaware of the current issues. At least I know how to work around it.


Thanks for stopping by, and as always - report those bugs! Please keep in mind that Discord (invite link: https://discord.gg/j4pZKuv) is the best way to report bugs. I don't always get notifications here on the steam forums and even when I look manually, some comments get buried for no reason until months later when they suddenly appear at the top. Strangely enough, this has been the case with several negative reviews for the game as well as a few bug reports. 
Facebook is a solid secondary way of reaching out (@ www.facebook.com/crossofauria), but occasionally I'll get notifications saying I have messages, but the messages won't be there. This was the case over the last few days, so if it was you that reported something on fb, I'm terribly sorry but FB won't let me see it.
And finally, Twitter should be the last case scenario in reporting bugs, as I generally never log into CoA's twitter. BUT, you can reach out to me directly @hardytier on twitter, which is one I actively log into all the time. (But seriously, if we can start using Discord for bug reporting, that would actually be the best for me personally >.>)

Anyway, that's it for this huge wall of text, thanks for stopping by, and I hope everyone enjoys their week!

//hardytier

notes.title: Mac Support
notes.content:
While preparing and testing the 3.2.1 patch, it has come to my attention that the game has become unstable, if not completely unplayable on certain versions of Mac operating systems. For that reason, 
Mac support is suspended indefinitely. 

I'll level with you all here for a minute - we were lucky to be able to release the game for Mac and Linux for as long as it was out there. A few months ago, the Linux builds became unpredictable, and now, I'm finally seeing that the Mac one has joined it. I'm not using a traditional engine in the creation of CoA like Unity or Unreal where I can code around and dig in and see what's going on. RMMV is an... all in one good luck to those who use it kind of endeavor. I work to create the game and updates on a windows desktop from which i export both a Windows build and a Mac build. For a long time, the mac build work. I can't say for sure when it stopped working since there were no reports, but I can confirm that as of today the project doesn't open at all. This -might- be because of when my version of RMMV stealthily updated from 1.5.1 to 1.6. Since I don't know when that was, I don't know how much of the project I would have to recreate from scratch in order to reincorporate Mac going forward. 

The short version of this: At some point in time, both the Linux and Mac exports from the engine broke. Windows support will continue for the time being with the schedule discussed a few weeks ago, but Mac and Linux will no longer receive updated builds.  I'm very sorry about this. If my understanding of Steam is correct, your key is still good to download the game on any windows machine or any virtual Windows OS with Steam on it.

I'm very sorry about this issue. If you have any suggestions, feel free to reach out.

//hardytier

Edit: 3:19PM APR 27
1. When the game is in its "completed" phase, I'll make all attempts I know how to in order to also port the game to both Mac and Mobile. Since these methods are very time consuming, they aren't worth attempting until production on the project comes to a close.

notes.title: 3.2.0 - Mass Skill Changes & New Character Skills!
notes.content:
This one is kinda huge, so I'll let the patch notes mostly speak for themselves. There is one major thing I will add though - The Orc War (or whatever I'll end up calling it at release) is officially in development! This build introduces 11 extra zones (3 new, 8 reskin for war purposes) in the background and functionality for one event in the Alpha Ruins. All of these will become available once the Orc War properly launches. 

[u][b]Note[/b][/u] - It may be possible in some way to slip yourself into one of the new zones. If you do, I strongly recommend backing up (or reloading from before then) - because you will be stuck there. The Orc War events will prevent other quest progression for the duration of the event. Aka; Rabbit's Foot and Phoenix Ash quests won't be complete-able until after. So if you find yourself triggering one of the new Orc War things, please let me know ASAP so I can patch it out until it's ready. 

[u][b]Note[/b][/u] - An incredible amount of background maintenance went into putting this one together, so things are bound to break. If anything breaks, the fastest way to reach me is through Facebook @ www.facebook.com/CrossOfAuria or through my personal discord in the CoA channels @ https://discord.gg/j4pZKuv.


[u][b]3.2.0 [Build #71, Release Date: April 26, 2020][/b][/u]
[b]New Skills![/b] – If your character has missed their chance to learn the skill, talking to the Delivery Boy in Auria will let the skills be learned.
- Alex has new skills between levels 3-16!
- Ruby has new skills between levels 9-17!
- Alex, Ruby, Miles, Riley each have a new level 22 skill!

[b]Fixes: [/b]
- The Lighthouse is now accessible once the quest is obtained through the Shoreline zone and now exits to the corresponding area in the same zone instead of onto the world map.
- Fixed drop rates for An’ura Taskmaster, An’ura Larvae, Cockatrice Minion, Cockatrice Menace, Spheria, and Oros tribe units.
- Fixed some passable tiles in the Restaurant set to now be impassable.

[b]Changes: [/b]
- All enemies with luck over 15 have had their Luck reduced by 75%.
-- This was done in an attempt to change the formula for determining successful escapes, but due to a plugin issue, luck cannot be factored into the equation. This might be solvable with a plugin update, but so much has the potential to explode that it is not worth the risk. Therefore…
--- It is now significantly easier to escape after each failed escape attempt. The base chance to escape remains the same.

[b]Skill Changes:[/b]
- Sticky Slap now receives a 0.25* bonus from Luck, down from 1.00*.
- Slap, Shot, Cut, Slash, Chop, Wing Slap, Ground Smash, Cutter, Double-Strike, Blade Shot, Charge, Gear Grind, Triple-Strike, Sting, Bloodfeast, Throw, Cleave, Swing, Cleave+, Insatiable Ravager, Rush, Disabling Slice, Silencing Slice, String Shot, String Scattershot, Swift Kick, Rapid Shot, Wicked Strike, Volley Shot, Suppression Blast, Slice, are now Physical type.
- Razor Wind is now Wind type.
- Rockbreaker is now Earth type.
- Point Laser, Laser Sweep, are now non-elemental.
- Poisonbolt no longer adds +6 to the damage formula.
- Frostbolt no longer adds +9 to the damage formula.
- Firebolt no longer adds +3 to the damage formula.
- Cost of Firebolt reduced to 10MP, down from 20MP to be in line with other tier 1 “bolt” spells.
- Cost of Fireball changed to 20MP, changed from 10MP + 20TP to be in line with other tier 2 “ball” spells.
- Details for Wild Charge (S:119) filled out.
- Poison Cut, Poison Chop, Poison Shot are now Poison type in addition to having a chance to inflict poison.
- Icefall no longer adds +3 to the damage formula [non-enraged only].
- Frostspike no longer adds +10 to the damage formula [non-enraged only].
- Lightning Rage’s “Attack” renamed “Spark Shock.”
- All Lightning Rage abilities now add +1 to Electric Power.
- Tooltip for Expose Weakness now accurately explains the effect.
- Expose Weakness now lasts for 5 turns and adds +5 to speed during use.
- Triple-Strike now costs 50 TP, up from 45.
- Arcane Missile now has a 2 turn warmup.
- Uppercut now has a 2 turn cooldown.
- Ruby no longer learns Triple-Strike at level 15.
- Insatiable Ravager now always inflicts a special attack-based bleed. Additionally, the chance to apply the other bleeds has been increased significantly. 
- Cost of Insatiable Ravager reduced to 50 TP from 100 TP. Additionally, this skill now has a 3-turn cooldown.
- Bloodthirst now gives Riley a chance to apply the Shatter debuff with basic attacks and other skills, which makes enemies more likely to be inflicted with various bleeds.
- Bloodthirst now has a chance to apply the new Insatiable Ravager bleed in addition to the 1%, 2%, 3%, 4% and 5% bleeds at varying rates.

[b]Plugins: [/b]
- Updated the BattleEngineCore, ActSeq1, ActSeq2, ActSeq3, X_AnimatedSVEnemies, BattleAICore, BattleStatusWindow, ItemCore, ItemUpgradeSlots, SkillCore plugins. With any luck, this should not affect current game files. This was done because at one point in time, my engine was automatically updated from 1.5.1 to the current build, which was not intentional. Reverting the engine itself may make the entire project unstable.

[b]What I Learned…[/b]
- The good news is, the Quest Log plugin works again. The bad news is, I already completely stripped all the related QL plugin code from the game, and it would take weeks to replace all of it. There may come a time in the future where I activate it moving forward, but it would not be worth anyone’s time for me to go apply it retroactively. The missive system will have to do.
- The TurnOrderDisplay is still broken no matter what I try to do with it. It broke right around the time the engine updated to 1.5.1 and never was able to come back since then. notes.title: 3.1.3.3 [Build #62, ActSeq Battle Fixes]
notes.content:
This week, a ton of work went into the new Lvell zones. As of right now, only guard NPCs have been made and placed. The interior of each structure is the current focus. However, it became apparent that I need to make a brand new trailer for the Steam Store page, so my focus shifted for the day. While gathering footage for the trailer, I came across a few issues that were missed from the addition of the new skills. The short story is: some of the battles in CoA, mostly "boss" style battles, use end of turn or even death attacks. These scripts interfere with the disappearing effect of the new attacks. For instance, Alex's Arcane Missile if it were to kill the Shield enemy in Agartha would cause the text boxes to be unreadable and members of the party to not appear until after Crash was used. A temporary fix for -some- of these issues is now in place, but a full playthrough of the game is necessary on my part to determine need-to-fix locations. In the meantime, I'll have to fix these on an as-I-notice-them basis. Feel free to report any oddities you may uncover!

Upcoming: 
3.1.4 will bring about the opening of the new Lvell zone, containing base dialogue and vendors for start-of-game and return to Lvell via Rabbit's Foot checkpoints. From there, 3.1.4.x will expand on the new zone, including quest additions to The Phoenix Ash and other things I'm both not sure of yet and not ready to reveal yet. Once the new Lvell zone is on par with other zones for the time being, 3.1.5 will come bringing the first elemental resistance technologies. It won't be possible for me to handle them as I originally planned, so instead of permanent aura's, we will be working with usable items similar to those available from StarSpear.

[u][b]Development Notes (Future Additions):[/b][/u]
[b][i]- “Frostfire” Set[/i][/b]
-- A new armor set with resistances to Fire and Ice is in the last stages of tweaking and will be available at the Black Forest vendor in (hopefully) the next update. Additionally, a new weapon type will be available for one of the party members at the same vendor. This set, in addition to gold, will require Congealed Fire and Congealed Frost to purchase.
-- Most of the data for this set is already finished and was released with this build.

[i][b]- Equipment Grading System: [/b][/i]
-- A new system is currently in development to make armor and weapons easier to inject into the game by grading entire sets with a point value and then distributing those point values percentagewise across the equipment slots. The working model distributes a set’s points by: 20% Head, 50% Chest, 10% Glove, 10% Boot, 10% Back. Additionally, this is further modified by equipment types with each stat (ATK/DEF/MAT/MDF/AGI/LUK/MHP/MMP) having a multiplier based on whether the piece of gear is Cloth, Leather, Mail, or Plate.
--- Example: A “25 point” def/mdf set would distribute 5 points to the headpiece, which would then divide those points with 70% (or 3.5 points) going to Defense and 30% (or 1.5 points) going to Magic Defense. These numbers would be further adjusted based on whatever the multiplier for each fabric type ends up being, which if Cloth had a 1* multiplier for Defense would result in 3.5 going into DEF, but a 0.5* multiplier for magic defense resulting in 0.75 going into MDF. 
--- NOTE1: The actual multiplier values for each stat relative to the equipment fabric type will be published alongside this system’s initial release with pictures or a tutorial video to make it significantly easier to understand.
--- NOTE2: The point value of sets will be released on a case by case basis, but it would be up to the players to figure out what the distribution would actually be, or simply pick up the items in game when available.
--- NOTE3: This system will not function retroactively for sets already in the game. Aka; no current items in game will have their values changed.

[i][b]- Lvell Expansion: [/b][/i]
-- A new section of Lvell is coming in an update soon which will feature 7 new structures, one of which is Lvell’s own Hunter Lodge! The Phoenix Ash will function similarly to the Rabbit’s Foot with quests that progress in level, difficulty, and complexity. The rewards are not yet set in stone, but Hunter Tokens will still come at the end of each quest and a vendor will be present to accept them in exchange for Phoenix Ash specific items and gear. 
-- Most of the data for this new section of the city has been released into the game with this build but is currently inaccessible.

[i][b]- An’ura Reconnaissance (Cont’d)[/b][/i]
-- The new An’ura-based questline introduced in 3.2 is still in development. Without spoiling too much, the goal is to create a “dungeon” expansion of the Den with challenging enemies and a twist ending. Additionally, a new friend may make use of the Arrowheads (this will be the only mention of that. Ever.) Dungeons will likely feature menu lockouts and save points – a throwback to some of my most favorite games of all time.

[i][b]- Hell’s Gate Ignited[/b][/i]
-- A new Hell’s Gate based questline with a hub and spoke layout is in pre-planning stages. The quest will begin in Sha’ri (bottom-right city).

[i][b]- The Orc War (Cont’d)[/b][/i]
-- The main story is still being worked on in the background and will most likely begin to roll out after An’ura Recon has concluded. Once the player embarks on the Orc War questline, they will not be able to return to the current state of the game for a short while. 

[i][b]- Agartha Activities[/b][/i]
-- The Pit’s extension to level 30 is in the planning stages pending main story enemy additions to the game.
-- There is no in-progress development regarding additions or changes to the Colosseum for the time being. Once the Orc War story is fully released, the next wave of Colosseum instances will enter development. From that point forward, these instances will be in some form of weekly rotation, with only one being available each week. The An’ura version will be brought to level 30 when it returns following the launch of the Scarlet version.

notes.title: 3.1.1.1 [Point of No Return]
notes.content:
Today, I continue to focus on removing old unused plugin commands. I planned on holding out to do another big patch, but then I discovered that Dixon and Dan's customized vendor situations broke the economy entirely. 

At this point, the 3.0.3.3 branch has been disabled but not deleted. In the event of an absolute dire emergency, it will be re-enabled. Until then, this 3.1.1.1 branch will serve as the new retreat point. This was done largely to prevent economy shattering. 

Turning our eyes to the real world for a minute, I've been able to do more recently due to the quarantine and shutdown. Ideally, I'll be able to make some more progress before it's all over. Don't forget! If you want to connect with me outside of these little patch notes, my Discord that is mostly used for my slow-moving streaming career is always open @ https://discord.gg/zsF6DD7

notes.title: 3.1.1 [Restructuring]
notes.content:
The key focus from this week's update is the internal item restructuring, which will leave some players who log in wondering what happened to the items they had. Rather than wipe out everyone's inventory, I've decided to leave them intact regardless of what items you may now have. This item change will make development easier on me moving forward, but may require a [b]new game file[/b] for you if you update to this version before getting to a point where you hold [b]no quest items[/b].
If you log in and decide that you need to roll back rather than restart, please use the following steps:
[u][b]Warning:[/b][/u] Please save on the world map before reverting to a previous version.
[b]Rollback Steps:[/b]
(1) – Right click Cross of Auria from the Steam menu.
(2) – Click “Properties”
(3) – Go to the “Betas” tab.
(4) – From the drop down menu, select 3.0.3.3 (which is the most stable recent build).
(5) – Complete any remaining quests which cause you to hold quest items.

notes.title: What's next for Cross of Auria?
notes.content:
In the June 2, 2019 progress update, I announced that I would be working on version 3.0 of the game and that it would be the final update. Here we are working up to a year later and I still haven't put it down. There's a few reasons for this. First and foremost, the story I wanted to tell, even the greatly abridged chapter 1 only version isn't yet complete (thank all of you for sticking with this super early access situation). Secondly, I wasn't quite sure yet how I wanted to proceed. I have so many notebooks full of ideas and files on my computer outlining Cross of Auria's episodic release along with Honor At Sea (which focuses on some of the other heroes in Revan just before the scourge). But I kept thinking to myself - is this the way I want to move forward? 

Well, the short answer is... no. As much as I would love to turn what we have here into some epic 1000 hour monster of a game, the technological limitations are too great. Plugins keep breaking and I keep having to reinvent the wheel when it comes to various systems because of their integration with now outdated or completely broken parts of the engine and plugin system. For a quick example, at some point last year we began running into an issue where the Quest Log text would completely disappear after the first save of the game. I have no idea when this began specifically and it wasn't caught until months later because it only affected the client side of the game and I do most tests on the engine side. Then we had a seemingly unimportant issue come up - the turn order display which shows you based on the attacks you've chosen who will go first.... well, that one just stopped showing altogether for reasons unknown and even reverting both the game and the engine to the working version didn't seem to correct the issue. It might have seemed small and meaningless, but it completely ruined my ability to focus on magic and abilities having individual speed values the way I wanted them to (think Quick Attack, Sucker Punch, etc from Pokemon) which would've made combat much more exciting. If you happened to be playing the game at that time, you may have noticed a difficulty spike in both the Flame Titan and the Frostbrood Titan. These were unintended consequences of the turn order display break. The difference between knowing when Flame Cutter is coming next turn or not is massive, don't you think? As such, both fights had to basically be crippled to be complete-able given the limited information that was now shown to the players. 

All unintended nonsense in the past, let's have a look at today. I'm basically at one of the same crossroads I was at when I initially wanted to move away from further development of CoA. The limitations of the engine put me in something of a rough spot - I can either continue to develop for something only a handful of people will ever see, or start to put in motion something on a more modern engine that might be able to gain traction even though the release time would be significantly longer. I'm looking at the latter as the way to go, but there's still some things in CoA that need to be wrapped up before I can look at it and say "ok, this is done." Let's talk a little bit about those things. 
[u][b]#1[/b][/u] - Complete the chapter 1 story. (Not to be confused with the episode 1 story, which is what is currently available). 
[u][b]#2[/b][/u] - Completely restructure the Items, Weapons, Armor, Skills so they fall in a more intuitive order when viewed in game. Specifically, I hate how the second wave of potions ended up so far down the list away from the first wave. You'd normally expect your pots to all be in one place, right? That's what I'd like to give for anyone tuning into the game later and for those of you still on it.
[u][b]#3[/b][/u] - Add more variety to the combat. This isn't as much of a difficult issue, as some of these changes will go live in the next update. Specifically, more types of attacks are being added to the existing enemies with a focus on Silence (prevents Magic) and Disable (prevents Abilities) - both of which will act as interrupts of they hit a character before the magic or ability is used. Also, and probably most importantly, moving of the Mend removal fight to before the Flame Titan as opposed to in Agartha. The reason for this is pretty much that it's too easy to just have Alex spam mend the entire time and get away without item usage in combat, or even strategic heal usage. 
[u][b]#4[/b][/u] - Release the prototype Battle Tower event in Agartha. If you've been on the game at the beginning and then again now, you may have noticed the bridge heading east in Agartha. This is where the Battle Tower will be, which was originally thought up as a standalone game. In it's CoA iteration, the idea will be to fight waves of bosses and handicaps to make it to the top of the tower and claim the prize. The Battle Tower standalone idea is significantly different from this straight up Ruby's party smash, but features the same enemy types.
[u][b]#5[/b][/u] - Finish the Quest Log removal and new Quest Missive integration. This will absolutely happen before development on CoA-E1 is concluded, even if nothing else on the list makes the cut.

Okay, so... that's my version of where we're at in the near future for CoA-E1. But what about Cross of Auria as a story or franchise or whatever it's going to be? The shortest version of what I'm thinking that I can say is - I'd love to see CoA come to live as an action RPG. Think Kingdom Hearts with significantly less cutscenes. I know enough about Unity and C# (having gotten a degree in using it and all) to build a prototype on my own and then crowdsource to build a complete product, but this will be an absolutely monumental undertaking for me and may take several years to release if it ever does come to fruition. This version of CoA ideally would not release episodically, but would release as a whole for Ruby's story. Jack, Katya, and Kara's stories would all then also be able to come to life in similar fashion. 

It's going to be a long road ahead, but this is definitely something I want to start doing, and there's no better time than right now. I sincerely want to thank all of you who have picked up Cross of Auria - Episode 1 and given it a try. I have so many more ideas that never made it into the game, but that's what happens when you're a one man team. I only have so many hands!


Alright, I know that was all super wordy, but I wanted to at least put it out there. The short version takeaway from this for all of you should be this:
- The next update will feature Silence and Disable as extra enemy statuses to be used against the players.
- The next several updates will continue the removal of the Quest Log dialogue ("questName has been added to the Quest Log!" and such) and replacement with the key item Missives. 

In the event I continue on CoA-E1 after that, the following are high on the docket:
- The restructuring of the Items, Weapons, Armor, and Skills, which would result in a complete item wipe-out for current players including all held and equipped gear.
- Severely reducing the amount of item drops per battle. Currently, it's way too easy to get gold and stay alive. I need to light a fire under your butts!

On that note, I'm off to work on adding Silence and Disable. Get ready for it out there in Revan, and all of you have a splendid rest of your week.

//hardytier

notes.title: 3.1.0.1 [Soul Fix / Quest Tracking]
notes.content:
This is a continuation of 3.1 with further terrain adjustments and the removal of the old Quest Log system. This process is still in progress and expected to take several more updates to complete. This update also fixes the Soul equipment type crash by removing it from the game. This equipment was meant to house elemental resistances, but I came up with a different and better way of handling it, so the Soul item is no longer needed. At this point, there were no equip-able Soul type items in the game, so only the equipment name was removed. Elemental resistance auras can be expected when the story continues which is after this wave of updates to what is currently in game. 

[b]On another note...[/b] I'm always looking for people to make any kind of content for CoA or try to "break" it so I can see what kinds of bugs still lurk. I'm a one man team of developer, so finding everything takes a great deal of time on my own. If you see something broken, please report it ASAP either here on Steam in the discussions, or preferably on facebook @ www.facebook.com/CrossOfAuria either by posting on the CoA wall or via DM. 
If you're a content creator, go ahead and drop your links to CoA videos on my fb DM!

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.content:
After the semi-explosion of the computer used to create CoA, there has been some down time. The good news that I'm here to announce is that progress was [u][b]not[/b][/u] lost! As soon as I am able, the final update (3.0) will begin development and be launched promptly after.

Most notably, 3.0 will:
- Permanently disable Achievement support across all platforms, as it currently does not work on Mac anyway and is untested on Linux.
- Replace the current Steam based achievement system with an in-game achievement system, viewable inside Ruby's House.
- Serve as the launch point from Episode 1 into Episode 2.

It is unlikely that I will be able to devote the time to releasing the planned Agartha activity in this episode, or provide a further update to the others. Short version on the reasoning why: the enemies are not yet decided or created. All the enemies you encounter in The Pit are enemies found naturally within the game, retaining their xp, gold, and loot drops. To make several (hundred, probably) more before the zones and levels of the next game are confirmed would be unwise, considering the planned change in level scaling and encounters.

When more information is available regarding CoA: Episode 2, you'll hear it here first!

notes.title: This Week In Revan (2.6.0 - Major Fixes & Adjustments)

Today, I've released a massive patch as the true beginning of the end. Most of the quests that were incomplete on the backend now are fully functional and ready to go. If you're already at the end of the game, The Rabbit's Foot has one more wave of quests ready to go! There's still going to be one final update to the Agartha activities, but after 3.0 releases, Episode 2 will begin development. If you're interested in the details of Ep. 2, reach out over facebook!

Anyway, here it is. If there's any issue at all, reach out over facebook ASAP.

Also.. a couple of side notes. 
- Episode 2 will [u][b]not[/b][/u] have Mac support. 
- Achievement support for Windows in this episode will be disabled with 3.0 and replaced with something at Ruby's House. Details TBA. 
- Episode 2 will [u][b]not[/b][/u] have achievement support unless otherwise specified. There seems to be a persistent issue between the system I use for achievements since one of the updates to the engine several months ago. 

[i]Current Known Issues:
- The Quest Journal text in the top left is disappearing after the first save and reload of the game. The cause for this is being investigated, but it is unlikely this issue will be resolved.
- Occasionally, the turn order display which shows characters and enemies during combat will only show the enemies. The cause for this is unknown.
- If you complete Ruby’s quest for Lightningstrike before going to the Veil for the third time, entering Frost Forest will show another prompt of completion.
- There are anomalies with the Pit version of the Frostbrood Titan. This is being looked into.
- If you encounter an error or any other oddity, please report it immediately @ www.facebook.com/CrossOfAuria.

notes.title: Update: Turn Order Display, Quest Log
notes.content:
After having spent the last two days working to repair these two plugins, I have concluded what I suspected.

1. The turn order display does not work in the Windows version of the game. It is unknown if it works on Mac or Linux, as I do not regularly test these builds.
2. The quest log becomes unstable after the first save of a new save file. Some parts become unreadable, and rarely - disappear altogether. 

I want to keep moving forward with the current game, but the change in structure from quest log to no quest log would be too jarring, I think. It may better suit me to recreate it altogether, or just move on to the next piece of the story.

[b]So here's what I've been working on...[/b]
It does not seem possible to recreate the game using an updated and expanded set of plugins as I want to. Ideally, I would just throw all of Yanfly's plugins together and use them as I learn them. Some issues are, not unexpectedly, arising from this approach. I may be able to use the current version of the game in the updated engine with select plugin additions moving forward. But then, I hit the wall when deciding what to do about the quest log. I've been back and forth with this for the past few days.

[b]What does this mean moving forward?[/b]
I think I can officially say that the next project won't contain the current first project. That is to say... the next game won't also include the entirety of the first game, which is both a good and a bad thing. I wanted to do this in chapters, but then I wanted to do it as one huge game, but then I hit a bunch of bugs and unfixable issues with plugins. It's been a hassle. The best thing for me is to make another short-ish (5-10 hours) story chunk similar to this game and see where we get from there. Ideally, at some point soon, I'll be able to begin development in Unity on a full-length RPG taking place in the same universe. That may be a ways away though.

[b]So... what does this all mean?[/b]
Let's cut right to it then, shall we?
1. Live support for Cross of Auria has officially ended. This means there will not be any future patches, content or bugfixes, unless something critically gamebreaking needs to be addressed. 
2. The activities in Agartha will not extend to the higher levels like originally intended. These activities may find their way into the next game in some form or another. They were all, including the unreleased one, extremely beneficial learning experiences for me that I truly hope I can share better in the future. 
3. This game in the store will be renamed "Cross of Auria: Episode 1" to reflect the changes. Additionally, the store page description will also see updates in the coming days.

That's all I've got for now. I truly hope each of you enjoyed what I was able to create in this first part of the story, and I hope to see you back in the next. Keep yourself posted by following @ www.facebook.com/CrossOfAuria to see when the next project goes live.

Until next time in Revan, my friends.

notes.title: 2.3.1.1 - The Bug Problem
notes.content:
We have run into a handful of very serious errors on the development side which is hindering progress. It's not the fault of the engine or the plugins, but mainly myself. I kept the plugins updated over time without regard for the fact that the engine itself has been updated. Ideally, i wanted this one game to span hundreds of quests and multiple stories. Sadly, I've hit a brick wall with that. Rather than continue with limited resources, I will be upgrading the engine and all plugins immediately. This may mean that updates for this game are no longer possible. The game, in my opinion, is in a good place. It took me about a year to make, and then another year and two months of live content updates and patches. I fully intend for the next game to come out swinging - building upon everything I learn here. I won't know whether or not I have to make a new project entirely until the engine is updated, but I'm preparing for the worst. If a CoA #2 does go into development, you'll know about it here first. If I'm able to reconstruct everything that breaks from the update, you'll also know that. Just be prepared.

[b]In addition to the following notes, a "this is the end" message appears upon triggering the second variation of the world map.[/b] Agartha and The Rabbit's Foot remain available after the second instance of the world map has been reached. Also, the 230special version of the game has been removed. Any player still using it will be reverted to the default branch.

[i]Current Known Issues:
- The turn order display at the top right is not displaying actors (your party). The cause for this is being investigated.
- The Quest Journal text in the top left is disappearing after the first save and reload of the game. The cause for this is being investigated.
- Some players are experiencing lag during the post-battle score screen or outright crashes. The reason for this was the January 2nd patch which saw the engine plugins updated. These issues should not occur in new save files. 
- If you encounter an error or any other oddity, please report it immediately @ www.facebook.com/CrossOfAuria.
2.3.1.1 [Build #38 Release Date: January 30, 2019]
Fixes: 
- The Market Town scene now prevents the player from leaving the others behind.
Changes: 
- Return bridges added to Hell’s Gate for after the Flame Titan has been defeated to make return trips less difficult.
Note: This may be the last update to CoA. Several unfixable bugs have been detected due to the engine version not being current but the plugins continuing to be updated for the newer version of the engine instead of the current. Gamebreaking bugs will still be addressed, but it will likely take some time to address them. The story of CoA is not yet finished – future games and comic-like releases are planned. It may be possible to update the engine and all plugins, but at this point I can’t promise that. Upon updating, many of the assets will become unusable, requiring entire zones and concepts to be restructured. Switches, variables, and transfers are all also likely to break. I will keep everyone posted with whatever information comes next.
[/i]

notes.title: Current Issues & Upcoming Fixes
notes.content:
Based on several YouTubers playing through the game, we have discovered a handful of pesky bugs which are in need of ironing out. Patches will roll out for each as soon as a fix is found.

As soon as I am able, I need to go through every little bit of the game again to see if I can manually trigger these issues to then repair them. This may take some time, and other updates are on the back burner until the test is concluded. Please keep in mind that the plugins were developed by a third party, and it may be that there is nothing I can do to fix these issues. If that's the case, the turn order display will be disabled and the quest journal will be left as is. It would be sad to do these things, but with them not working properly, there's no other alternative, as removing the plugins altogether would require a new game file for every player. I believe the quest log to be an integral part of the game, even with this minor hiccup. 

Videos will follow on the CoA YouTube channel explaining all of this, including what to expect regardless of which way forward we go.

[i]Current Known Issues:
1. [u][b]Turn Order Display[/b][/u] -  The turn order display at the top right is not displaying actors (your party). The cause for this is being investigated.
2. [u][b]Quest Journal[/b][/u] - The Quest Journal text in the top left is disappearing randomly during gameplay. The cause for this is being investigated.
3. [u][b]EXP/Loot Screen[/b][/u] - Some players are experiencing lag during the post-battle score screen or outright crashes. The reason for this was (probably) the January 2nd patch which saw the engine plugins updated. These issues should not occur in new save files. 
- If you encounter an error or any other oddity, please report it immediately @ www.facebook.com/CrossOfAuria.
[/i]

On another note, the next content update is also being worked on. The highlight of 2.3.2 is the Hall of Challengers activity being raised in difficulty to level 30, up from it's current level of 10. Levels 1-10 have 3 possible enemy groups per battle. Levels 2-30 have 2 possible variations. As always, there will be more to the update, but we'll save that for update day. Until then, good luck out there, and keep those bug reports coming! You never know which might be the one to fix everything.
As always, the roadmap may change or be canceled for any reason. Updates will be available here first, then on facebook or youtube.

Also, if you happen to pinpoint the exact moment the Quest Journal bugs out, please let me know ASAP! I'll also be looking for it here on my end.

P.S. - The 230special variant of the game will remain active until the next patch.

notes.title: 2018 Year End Update
notes.content:
(Skip to the bottom for bullet points)
Exciting news, everyone! There are now more than 400 people who own Cross of Auria! The continued growth of CoA comes as a delight at a time when I'm contemplating what comes next. So, let's dig in a little bit.

I consider the first chapter (everything currently in the game) to be as complete as it can be at this stage and with the free time I have in terms of the story, but there's a lot that still needs to be done. I'm not going to spoil too much of it, but keep your eyes on the Cross of Auria official YouTube page (at https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCGxc2-7sJbZ9L3Lpgak43XA ) for more detailed visual information.

What I can tell you... There is much more to go! My initial vision saw this game with at least 1,000 quests and functioning as an open world. I still plan to accomplish this, but it's taking time. In the more immediate future, I have planned another activity in Agartha. The storyboarding is almost finished, and development will not take too long once it begins. A greatly expanded version of this activity is planned for release on iOS/Android for 2019. This mobile release will take place outside the linear confines of the CoA story. 

That's all for now, expect more updates (patch notes or otherwise) in the next few weeks once my schedule from the holidays frees up.

Summary:
• Playable events from start of game to before Veil 3 considered finalized unless bugs are discovered moving forward.
• The third iteration of the Veil may see more added to it soon, so be sure to keep a pre-Veil save.
• Another activity will be coming to Agartha in the next few weeks. This will serve as an Alpha test for a planned mobile app set to be released in 2019. 
• Kara's story is being written. More on that soon.
• Additions to The Pit and the Colosseum are in the brainstorming phase. It would greatly help to see some of you in your attempts to clear these activities - so feel free to reach out at www.facebook.com/CrossOfAuria with any YouTube videos you've made regarding anything CoA, especially the Agartha activities!
• Much more is being planned, but I won't share it until we're closer to a release. 
• The next patch may see a reduction in storage requirements, provided I can set it up the right way.

notes.title: This Week In Revan (2.1 - How to Say Goodbye)
notes.content:
[u][b]Patch Notes[/b][/u]
2.1 [Build #27, Release Date: November 30, 2018]
New: 
- The story continues! Players are able to progress completely through the game up to the end screen and beyond. 
Fixes:
- Removed several high res images to reduce game size.
Other: 
- Quest - Rayman’s Grief removed. If you currently have this quest, it will be removed from your quest log upon completing the game.
Notes: 
- This is the last content update for Cross of Auria – The Awakening. For more details, please go to www.facebook.com/CrossOfAuria. Further bug fix patches may be released as necessary.

[u][b]Update[/b][/u] - Let's Talk
There was so much more I wanted to add to this project before I closed the doors on it. So many ideas that came into being midway through development, like the elemental drawing system from nodes in the world, and of course - the pit and colosseum. Once I got into the final months of college, my free time to work on this came to a screeching halt. I went slowly from weekly updates, to monthly, to none at all. That is why I felt it best to end the game the way it is as of this patch today. The decision to end it here is largely financial, and is just one step in growing up as a person, a writer, and even a game designer. It's time for the next idea, and I hope to see all of you there.

However... you should know that this story is not abandoned. It is not over. I am just looking into new ways to move it forward, while keeping true to my original promise to never increase the price above its original $0.99USD. You will hear more from Revan.

Future patch notes will only include details of the bug fixes. No future update to Cross of Auria - The Awakening will contain significant content the way others have in the past.

As always, stay safe, have a good time, and join me over at www.facebook.com/CrossOfAuria for future updates into the CoA universe.

hardy out.

notes.title: 2.0.1 - Minor Fix & Update
notes.content:
2.0.1: Removed several high res images to reduce size of game (~500MB).

[u][b]Update: [/b][/u]
I have some good news and some bad news. 
The good news is - the new computer is here and I will be able to continue the story much more efficiently from here on out!
The bad news is... I have to wrap up this chapter of the story (The Awakening) sooner than originally intended. Not all of the files were able to survive the transfer to the new computer in a way that will allow me to continue working on the current project on it. I will need to completely re-find and acquire all assets that do not come standard with RPG Maker MV for the next installment (CoA Chapter 2). In the meantime, I will finish The Awakening on my old computer, with preference to ending the story to be moved forward rather than to add content.

For my first solo creation, I think this was a success. There is roughly 8 hours of play time for a new player and I was able to test a lot of ideas that will go forward into the next chapter, next installment, or next project. 

As of right now, expect the deadline to remain Dec 31st, 2018 for the last update to this game, but it may come sooner. Thank you everyone who has been a part of the CoA community and given me the drive to keep going!

As always, for more updates, especially starting in 2019, check out the facebook page www.facebook.com/CrossOfAuria instead of here on Steam, as opposed to in addition to like it currently is.

And on that note, I'll see you in the next one!

notes.title: This Week In Revan (2.0 Preparation)
notes.content:
With college coming to an end for me, it's time to buckle up and finish the project that is the first [i]Cross of Auria[/i] game. This chapter, known as [i]Cross of Auria - The Awakening[/i] is about to endure heavy additions following the point we last left off - Frost Forest. From here, you as the player will now be able to return to Auria and enter the Castle Grounds North area to begin the next part of your adventure. That being said, I am abandoning the following mechanics (for this game only) in favor of finishing the story:
- Elemental absorb nodes. (Current ice nodes will remain in the game, but no more will be added.)
- Black Forest puzzle (sound puzzle will still play, but completing it will no longer take you to the secret area).
- Rank II is the final wave of quests from The Rabbit's Foot for this game and will be shipped with the remaining pieces of the game.

My initial goal for CoA was to have one huge game that encompassed all ten (or more) chapters of the story I was writing. However, due to time restrictions, that idea is no longer viable. Once I graduate, I may no longer have the time to support a project like this in terms of frequent patching, which is why the subsequent games will not be released as living projects as this one has. They will be released as complete products and will only receive patches to fix things that are game-breakingly broken, with the goal being to put out the entire story above all else. 

This game was an experiment for me as a future game designer regarding my ability to create zones, design a skill and item system, create interesting boss mechanics, and write a story. In my time making this, I've learned a great deal about RPG Maker in general, and in general how to make systems and maps. I look forward to using this, and other engines in the future, to create the next chapters in the [i]Cross of Auria[/i] series.

Now that the sentimental part of this is over, let's talk about how we're going to wrap up [i]Cross of Auria - The Awakening[/i]...

{2.0.0.0, Build #25 [b]Preview[/b]}
[i]Note: All of the following is done with consideration to finishing the main story of CoA and finishing overall development of this chapter.[/i]
#1) The Colosseum and The Pit will be extended to include up to level 25 opponents. This is due to the player level being capped at 20.
#2) Puzzle zones are locked. (Black forest, ruins of alpha, etc).
#3) Colosseum will not feature other dungeons as originally intended. - This was an experimental section that would have expanded based on reception. It will return in some way in the future games and will remain available in this one.
#4) Achievements will be scaled down to include what is currently available (at the time of 2.0 release).
#5) Lvell will reopen as part of The Orcs of Revan questline. It is at this point you can complete the corresponding Rabbit's Foot quest in the area.
#6) Obscurite, the Dusk Kingdom (the area north of Frost Forest) was in development for several weeks, but is not scheduled to make an appearance in this game at this time. The data for this and other zones still remain in the game, so it is still possible to find your way through the cracks.
#7-?) And more to come, with heavy focus on progressing the main story.

As it has been before, updates will release in small chunks until the game is completely finished, which I'm aiming to be before the new year. This project was first released on new years day, it's only fitting it be completed before the next.

And with that, I'll see you in the patch notes. As always, feel free to reach out on Facebook @ facebook.com/CrossOfAuria.

//hardytier

notes.content:

notes.title: This Week in Revan (1.1.0.2 Update)
notes.content:
1.1.0.2 [Build #14]
New:
- Teleport pads added to The Black Forest.
-- These pads can be discovered after the Inn scene in Auria.

- The first vents have appeared in Frost Forest!
-- Combine essences at an alchemist table to create bottled magic! Then, throw them at your enemy!
--- The first table will make its appearance in 1.1.0.3. 
--- Until then, a makeshift mixing kit will appear in The Rabbit's Foot for players who carry essences and have completed all tier 1 hunts.
-- Vents reset after each boss fight moving forward in the story, and after each level 10+ rift.

- Prototype "Endless" mode added to the Hall of Challengers!
-- You may end the Endless mode by successfully escaping from a battle or by being defeated. 
-- Endless mode currently includes the battles from levels 7 to 10 of the original version of the pit. 
-- As the normal pit is updated with higher level enemies, so to will the Endless mode.

Fixes: 
- Random encounters added to Frost Forest.
- Music added to Frost Forest.
- Transfer sound added to Den An'ura for return visits.

Other:
- The way music plays from scene to scene has been changed.
-- If a zone does not play music upon entering it, exiting and re-entering should fix the issue.
-- Issue should not exist for new save files.

1.1.0.3 preview:
Continuation of Pre-Emptive Strike.
Keeping the goal on 1.1.0.3 narrow in order to progress the story and edit some of the back end to make creating new pieces easier, and overall to have those pieces take less time to produce.

notes.title: This Week in Revan (1.1.0.0 Update)
notes.content:
Over the last few weeks, I've been preparing the next part of chapter 1 - The Orc War. It's been a long ride so far and there's still a long way to go.  I've made some changes to the pieces currently in the game, but nothing too big. New players will now be able to enter The Elcott Mansion, which is the house next to Ruby's. Several doors have been sealed off until their story relevance is revealed. And of course, there were a number of bug fixes.

Moving on to what's new... Frost Forest is currently in development. This will be the area north of Auria. It will be made in a similar fashion to The Black Forest, in that each tile on the map (tile = 1 player step) will be expanded into a small zone. I don't want to give the goods about FF, but I want to let you in on the idea. This part of the game has somewhat of a minigame idea that I have rolling around in my head that I wanted to test out. The player basically needs to find something, then do something. From there, the effect of the player's action will remain for the duration of the game. 

About what I've been doing (in real life)... I've been absolutely swamped with school, which is why the updates slowed down. However, I will be putting out a new update every weekend with any finished content - just to keep the ball rolling. For those of you that have been playing through, I'm going to work on expanding Agartha's challenges to really test you.

Preview: 1.1.0.1
- The goal for 1.1.0.1 is to remove the restrictions in Frost Forest to allow players to access the event. 

That being said, here are the patch notes for 1.1.0.0 (The Orc War - Setup Phase)

[b][u]1.1.0.0 [Build #12][/u][/b]
* The engine used to build Cross of Auria has been updated, prompting the update of several plugins. You may need to 
	start a new game to prevent errors in the save file. Until the game is finished, we may run into this issue 
	from time to time, thought it won't be often. 
* This is the first of a weekly update series. See https://www.facebook.com/CrossOfAuria for more information.

Fixes:
- Girl in Rabbit's Foot will give Ruby the skill Sparkstrike if you missed it in Scarlet Cavern.
- First dialogue in Frost Forest will give Ruby Sparkstrike if missed in both Rabbits Foot and Scarlet Cavern.
	- These updates are temporary, and will be removed in a future update.
- Scarlet Cavern Ogre fight reconfigured to prevent players from missing the Sparkstrike event. 
- Fixed an error for Linux users during the Jack tutorial battle.

Updates:
- Frost Forest is in development.
	- Players can enter the first zone of Frost Forest to increase the level cap to 15.
	- As the zones become finished, they will be released as part of the weekly update. Roadblocks will be in place
		to prevent players from accessing unfinished story-based areas.
- Most plugins have had their versions updated, and may function better for it.
- Dialogue added to Cadets and Adventurers after the meeting scene in Auria.
- Dragonbones related encounters (animated enemies) have been removed due to a compatibility error.
- Minor changes to the Veil #1.
- Minor changes Lvell/Corner District (Ruby's House & The Elcott Mansion). 
- Minor changes to Lvell/Outer Town and the houses contained in that area.
- Minor shadowing from start to HG.
- Professor Dixon now stays in the Frostbrood Lair until the player drops down to the exit.
- Fixed an issue with Schematic: Green Insect Wand.
- Green Insect Wand now grants Alex access to An'ura Spore.

notes.title: Update Delay
notes.content:
The engine used to create Cross of Auria pushed an update (RPG Maker v1.6), causing many of the plugins used to stop functioning as expected. As of right now, we're waiting on Yanfly (the dude who makes all the amazing plugins) to push updates that will make them compatible with the engine update. Until then, I can't push any patches, or everything will break. 

If you find any new bugs, please let me know ASAP as a reply to this message or via facebook @ https://www.facebook.com/CrossOfAuria. 

The following bugs will be addressed in 1.1.0.0:
- Missable Sparkstrike: If you get really lucky during the Ogre fight with Jack in Scarlet Cavern, you can kill it before Ruby learns Sparkstrike. To fix this, the fight has been reconfigured to give the Ogre the Immortal status until Ruby learns Sparkstrike. For those that have already missed Sparkstrike, it can be acquired by talking to the girl (not the Hunter) in The Rabbit's Foot, or by entering the first zone of Frost Forest (when it becomes available). 

- Fixed an error for Linux users during the Jack tutorial battle.

Updates in 1.1.0.0:
- Level cap will rise to 15 for players who enter Frost Forest.
- The Rabbit's Foot design will change for players who completed all of the tier 1 quests. Professor Dixon has joined the lodge for the time being, and will also offer quests.

Important info: Once the updates from Yanfly are all in place, there will be weekly updates to CoA. Each update may not contain a completely finished area, but each update will build upon the last from now until the game is complete. 

I'll announce either here or via facebook when the updates will start rolling out. Thank you all for your support!

//hardytier

notes.title: What's Next? (Feb 15th Update)
notes.content:
Want to see what I've been working on? Check it out here: https://youtu.be/hTGsqHHag4I

The first version of the Hall of Challengers is live!

Visit HoC in Agartha, to the left of the Colosseum. 

HoC provides a new challenge to players as they level up, as well as providing a fast xp and item grind. 

While there are no direct rewards for completing any version of HoC so far, all enemies fought have the same drop rates as they did the first time you met them, minus special story items. This includes XP and special coins.

HoC will serve as somewhat of a "horde mode" as the story progresses, and will be updated regularly with the Colosseum. However, events in the Colosseum expire over time. The progression through HoC will remain available forever.

In a future update, HoC will feature a true max level horde mode, where the player will fight battles until the party is knocked out.

Death in the Pit is not permanent, but you still might want to save before entering.

Good luck!

//Hardytier

HoC provides a new challenge to players as they level up, as well as providing a fast xp and item grind. 

While there are no direct rewards for completing any version of HoC so far, all enemies fought have the same drop rates as they did the first time you met them, minus special story items. This includes XP and special coins.

HoC will serve as somewhat of a "horde mode" as the story progresses, and will be updated regularly with the Colosseum. However, events in the Colosseum expire over time. The progression through HoC will remain available forever.

In a future update, HoC will feature a true max level horde mode, where the player will fight battles until the party is knocked out.

Death in the Pit is not permanent, but you still might want to save before entering.

Good luck!

//Hardytier

Version 1.0.1.0 of the game is set for release Sunday, January 7th @ 9:00AM Eastern time. 1.0.1.0 will include the level 10 rift as well as an update to the Warden's shop. Any other bug fixes between today, Jan 4, and Jan 7 will be deployed along with 1.0.1.0. 

Following 1.0.1.0, the next part of Agartha will undergo construction to bring about a new end-game zone that will persist and be updated through all iterations of the game.

Chapter 1-2: "The Scourge - The Orc War" begins development now!

//hardytier

notes.title: Release Announcement
notes.content:
"As some of you may know, I’ve been working on a game in a classic RPG style engine (RPG Maker MV) as a stepping stone into the gaming industry. I have two primary goals for this project – to have a released project for my portfolio before I graduate, and to establish the groundwork for a new comic book style universe that I’ve been working on. On to the more formal part of this…

I’m incredibly proud to introduce the upcoming release of Cross of Auria! In Januar, 2018, this game will launch for Windows on Steam for $0.99 and will have free story-based updates over time. While I have established a Patreon page (found at https://www.patreon.com/hardytier), I will not be charging for any DLC or updates for the life of the game. Cross of Auria will serve as the baseline to introduce a new universe of characters that will (hopefully) extend into other games, comics, and/or web series’. That’s right, I basically have the idea for a full franchise. I know that’s a far off dream right now, but I’m hoping that with everyone’s help, I can make it all a reality. Support for Mac, iOS & Android TBA after initial release.

Now the part about what I want from you… Play the game! Leave a review! Comments, suggestions, feedback, etc. That’s all I need to get moving. Success or failure, I need this for my future as a game designer. But if we have to choose, let’s make it a success!
Thank you for taking time out of your busy day to read this. I hope to be hearing from you soon.


Contact Info:
CoA Steam Page: http://store.steampowered.com/app/764180/Cross_of_Auria/
CoA Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/CrossOfAuria/ (All updates to be posted here!)
Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/hardytier
Twitter: https://twitter.com/hardytier"

Copied from CoA's official facebook page.


In addition to the above, I would like you all to know that I am looking for an artist for Steam icons. In the future, I'll be looking for background and other images. Please @ me on twitter if interested.
